sources: JSC 37461 STS-134 Mission Report (Sep 2011): events Appendix A; SSME 104.5% and single-step 72% bucket
STS-134 MOD FRR Flight Design (Mar 2011): insertion 122 nm / 51.6 deg, 170 s OMS assist, DOLILU II
notes: IYD: the ISS's own plane at SRB ignition, Earth-fixed: from the ISS two-line elements of 2011 day 136.48289737 (Space-Track, NORAD 25544): inclination 51.6484, node 323.5050 regressing -5.1476 deg/day -> 323.2151 at 136/12:56:27.994, less GMST 68.0094 = 255.2057 deg east.  CGGB_EF_PLANE_SW is ON, so GG2ASC freezes it into M50 at the predicted liftoff.  The pad was 44.8 nmi (0.75 deg) off this plane at liftoff -- about five minutes from the in-plane time, inside the MOD FRR's window 'centered at in-plane'; guidance steers the rest, as on the real flight.  (The first DOLILU assumed an in-plane launch: the 51.6-deg plane through the pad, 0.97 deg from this one.)
THROT is INTEGER: 104 for the flight's 104.5
Message 37 is the tape's own 58 halfwords with the named fields changed; masses in slugs, the orbiter-dependent ones moved by the STS-134 orbiter's difference from the tape's 203,193 lb

First stage: PSI/PHI/QPOLY/TREF from the simulated stack, not from the flight's own (unavailable) DOLILU: the yaw table turned to the 51.6-deg azimuth and the throttle velocities placed at the report's throttle times

Message 11, the wind table: STS-134's measured winds (FSSR Table 4.2-1 lists WNDE_TAB/WNDN_TAB as DOLILU parameters).  First-stage guidance subtracts them from the relative velocity to index the pitch and yaw tables by the aerodynamic reference velocity VREL_AERO_REF (GG31ST, FSSR 4.2.3), so the tables must be shaped with this wind in place.  The truth model flies the same sounding (YAGPC_VEHDYN_SOUNDING).

Wind sources: PASS's table (message 11) is the 12Z Cape sounding (74794), the last balloon before launch in the University of Wyoming archive (released ~11:00Z; nothing earlier is archived for 74794 on 15-16 May 2011, and the ground's own DOLILU winds -- Jimsphere and the 50 MHz profiler, prepared hours ahead -- are not available).  The truth flies the air at launch: 12Z and 15Z interpolated to 12:56Z (sts134-sounding-74794-20110516-1256Z.csv).  Between 12Z and 15Z the westerly at 10-12 km strengthened 7-11 m/s, matching JSC 37461's 'late predicted change in the wind at approximately 30,000 to 40,000 ft'; density changed < 1%.

fields.name: PSI(1-30): the tape's 38-deg table turned by -28.71 deg: -18.71 for the inertial azimuth (63.66 -> 44.95), and -10 found by flight -- the first stage then ends 18 nmi out of the final plane instead of 29, the MECO target is reached (-18 and -26 fall short) (PSI = tan(yaw/4), GG31ST.hal step 16)

THET(1,1-30), tan(theta/4): shaped by flight to STS-134's ASCENT ADI - NOMINAL cue card (Ascent Checklist CC 10-11, ASC-14a/134; the same on every OI-34 flight's card): H 10/27/51/85/126 kft, Hdot 670/1007/1441/1902/2200 ft/s at T+30/50/70/90/110. RE-SHAPED 2026-10-05 for the day's winds and atmosphere (message 11, the 12:56Z sounding): +1.0 deg at Vrel 190-963 ft/s, -0.5 at 1,104, -2.8 at 1,378, -3.6 to -3.8 at 1,587-2,801, easing to -1.5 from 4,030 (flights t1-t4). Flight t4f: 9.0/26.2/50.8/85.6/126.9 kft, 659/1020/1491/1911/2162 ft/s; bucket 72% at T+39.40-51.24 (STS-134 39.5-51.3; QPOLY and TREF 21.4 unchanged, adaptive throttling off); second stage within ~5 kft of the card from Vi 7,000 on (was +22.6 kft at Vi 6,000). Before, with the day's weather (s1): 8.9/25.9/50.4/85.6/128.3 kft, 653/1010/1489/1959/2250 ft/s. THET is applied before the yaw turn and load relief takes several degrees at max-q, so it runs well above the flown pitch. Was the tape's table with the pitch-over scaled 0.88 (max-q ~950 psf).
PHI(1-15): the same turn at liftoff (PHI(1) = PSI(1): no roll on the pad), blended out by heads-down 180 deg

WNDE_TAB(1-8), ft/s toward east, at ALT_WND 0/8/18/28/38/48/58/80 kft: the Cape Canaveral sounding 74794 of 2011-05-16 12Z (University of Wyoming archive; sts134-sounding-74794-2011051612Z.csv), an hour before launch, averaged over +-1,000 ft. The tape's: 0/-36/-67/-107/-151/-122/-48/0
WNDN_TAB(1-8), ft/s toward north, the same sounding. The tape's: all 0

QPOLY(1-4): Vrel ft/s where THROT(J) applies -- the simulated vehicle's (pitch table of message 13) Vrel at STS-134's throttle times T+4.1, 39.5, 51.3 s (JSC 37461 App. A); flight p8: 72% from T+39.9 to T+51.7

TREF_ADJUST: the simulated vehicle reaches VREF_ADJUST 488 ft/s at T+21.15 (with STS-134's faster SRBs) and guidance sees it on its next pass (~0.27 s); 21.4 keeps TDEL inside the 0.21 s deadband, so adaptive throttling stays off as on STS-134 (JSC 37461: single-step bucket to 72%, AGT not activated).  Re-measure whenever the first stage changes: the QPOLY span is 232 ft/s, so 0.3 s outside the deadband moves the bucket by ~8%.
GAMD 0.65 deg, as the tape reconfiguration's FPA_NOM (sts134-reconfig.json)

fields.name: IYD_OMS(1): the STS-134 plane (PEG 4 flies the present orbit's plane regardless, GGILTV step 31)
OMS 1: DTIG, HT, THETA, C1, C2 -- the tape's; STS-134 did not need OMS 1 (JSC 37461 Appendix A)

OMS 2: TIG = ET separation + 1,756 s (STS-134: ET sep MET 8:42, OMS-2 TIG MET 37:58); an apsis 175.8 nmi high at theta T 330.43 deg, designed with omstarget.py on a simulated post-MECO orbit (28 x 125 nmi) -- a pre-flight value: fly_sts134.py's ground redesigns and uplinks it after MECO from the actual insertion, as Mission Control did
